findings.evidence: FINAL_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:108 (the report's current-state block, verdict 'DEMO-READY ACADEMIC MVP') states in the present tense: 'Le code n'a plus de P2 connu non traité, hors le choix de conception A-02' and that the exit criteria are met, with the exit criterion being 'zéro P2 sur l'état audité en dernier' (GOAL_FINAL_MVP.md:21,31). The report's round table stops at tour 30 and never mentions rounds 31-34 (grep 'tour 34|r34|r31' in the report = no hit). But docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:135-143 ('Round 34 notes') says the last audited state (round 34, code unchanged since 12:21) has P2 = 7 and 'All items below are open and unfixed', among them code defects: B-001 (last correct step's explanation not rendered), A-001/C-004 (two competency definitions), A-002 (hint double charge, no idempotency key), A-003 (seed-demo guard case-sensitive), C-001, C-002, C-003. reports/test-e2e/r34/round-1/wave-{A,B,C}-findings.json sum to 0/0/7/19 (recomputed). findings.evidence: be/README.md:68: 'Teacher "success" of a mission is the class mean of that accuracy (missions under 70% are flagged, the lowest is the hardest)'. Code and the published rule say otherwise: game.ts:1047-1048 flags only `hardest` and only if < 70, rules.ts:17 'The server flags only the hardest mission (the lowest success), and only when it falls under 70%'. Live (class 1, 50 students, scratch API :3701): Acid-Base Emergency 62% shows 'Needs attention'; Gram Stain Challenge 66% (also under 70) has no flag in the UI (main text lists 'Gram Stain Challenge / 30 of 50 students completed / accuracy 66%' with no badge) and the API has needsAttention false for it.

findings.state_artifact: scratch class 'Round Two' (id 7) and 'Acc Two'; shot C35-rounding-completion-34pct.png
findings.evidence: Class aggregates are means of already-rounded per-student values (game.ts:1065-1066 `mean(roster.map(r=>r.progressPct))`, `mean(withAcc.map(r=>r.accuracyPct))`) while per-lab/per-mission figures are rounded once. Recomputed from raw SQLite tables with exact fractions: class of 2 students (0 missions, 6 missions): API cohort.avgCompletionPct = 34 (rows show 0% and 67%), raw 6 of 18 missions = 33.3% -> 33; avgMissionsCompleted printed by the same payload = 3 (= 33%). The 'Completion 34%' tile therefore contradicts 'average 3 of 9 missions'. Class of 2 students with accuracy 100% and 1/6 (hem-01 with 5 wrong): API cohort.avgAccuracyPct = 59 vs exact (1+1/6)/2 = 58.33 -> 58, whereas the same payload's labs[hematology].accuracyPct is 58 (single rounding). Brute force: 12 of 55 two-student completion pairs and 26 three-student triples differ by 1 point.
findings.fix_hint: Compute cohort percentages from raw sums (sum of missions / (9 x students); mean of unrounded accuracies) and round once.

findings.evidence: Float artefact on an exact .5: three students on Blood Smear Code with 5, 7 and 11 wrong answers have accuracies 1/6, 1/8, 1/12 whose exact mean is 12.5%. API missions[hem-01].successPct = 12, labs[hematology].accuracyPct = 12, hardestMission.successPct = 12 (Math.round(100*sum/n) with sum = 0.37499999..). Round-half-up of the exact value (and of the displayed row values 17/13/8 -> 12.67 -> 13) gives 13. Found by exhaustive search (Math.round vs exact rational half-up: 101 mismatching combinations of 2-4 missions, 4 for equal-mission classes of up to 3 students) and confirmed live; independent recompute of the 50-student class and 4 other classes: 0 other differences.
findings.fix_hint: Compute with integer arithmetic (n*100*den) or add an epsilon / use toFixed-free exact rational before rounding.

findings.state_artifact: be/src/routes.ts (POST /api/auth/demo limiter 60 per 10 min per IP) vs be/.env.example, docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md, be/README.md
findings.evidence: POST /api/auth/demo is limited to 60 calls per 10 minutes per IP (routes.ts: limiter.hit(`demo:${c.ip}`, ... 60, 600_000) outside NODE_ENV=test). The browser calls it once per new tab/session and once per guest switch (verified: load=1, reload=0, Faculty guest=+1). It is listed nowhere: .env.example 'Rate limits (defaults in parentheses)' omits it, KNOWN_LIMITATIONS items 9/11 (shared NAT) omit it, and the demo script never mentions it. Live: after ~60 calls the next page load shows 'Demo laboratory unavailable ... Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.' (shot C35-demo-signin-429.png). A class behind one NAT opening the demo link (>60 sessions in 10 minutes) is blocked.
findings.fix_hint: Document the demo budget (and that RATE_* does not tune it) in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS and the demo script's 'multi-visitor' warning, or make it configurable.

findings.state_artifact: Content review, 401 during a status change; shot C35-401-midaction-lands-on-analytics.png
findings.evidence: Two tabs; in tab B the stored token is invalidated, then 'Approve' is clicked on Content review. The app silently opens a new faculty guest session, drops the click and lands on 'Class intelligence' (Faculty analytics), with the blue notice 'Your faculty guest session expired, so a new faculty guest session was opened.' It does not say that the status change was NOT applied (server confirms: content_audit has no row for it) and does not return to Content review, so a reviewer may believe the approval went through. 409 (stale tab), lost response (route.fetch then abort), lost response + offline + Retry, Enter/Space/double-Enter paths were all correct (row refreshed from the server, 'Could not confirm...' alert, one audit row per real transition, focus kept on the next action).
findings.fix_hint: Append 'Your last action was not saved' to the session-renewed notice when a mutation was in flight, and keep the user on the current view.
